units.zh: 嗚呼，盛衰之理，雖曰天命，豈非人事哉！
units.en: Alas! Rise and fall may be called fate—but is it not, in the end, the work of men?
units.literal: Alas! The principle of rise and decline—though called Heaven’s mandate—is it not rather human affairs!

units.zh: 原莊宗之所以得天下，與其所以失之者，可以知之矣。
units.en: Consider how Zhuangzong won the realm and how he lost it—the answer lies there.
units.literal: Tracing why Zhuangzong gained the realm and why he lost it, one may know this.

units.zh: 世言晉王之將終也，以三矢賜莊宗而告之曰：「梁，吾仇也，燕王吾所立，契丹與吾約為兄弟，而皆背晉以歸梁。
units.en: Men say that as the Prince of Jin lay dying he gave Zhuangzong three arrows and said: “Liang is my foe; the Prince of Yan I raised up; the Khitan and I were sworn brothers—yet all turned from Jin to Liang.
units.literal: The world says when the Prince of Jin was near death he gave Zhuangzong three arrows and told him: “Liang is my enemy; the Prince of Yan I myself established; the Khitan and I swore brotherhood—all yet betrayed Jin to join Liang.

units.zh: 此三者，吾遺恨也。
units.en: These three are the debts I leave unpaid.
units.literal: These three are my remaining hatreds.

units.zh: 與爾三矢，爾其無忘乃父之志！」
units.en: Take these three arrows—do not forget your father’s charge!”
units.literal: I give you three arrows—you must not forget your father’s will!”

units.zh: 莊宗受而藏之於廟。
units.en: Zhuangzong took them and laid them in the ancestral temple.
units.literal: Zhuangzong received them and stored them in the temple.

units.zh: 其后用兵，則遣從事以一少牢告廟，請其矢，盛以錦囊，負而前驅，及凱旋而納之。
units.en: Whenever he marched to war he sent a clerk with a young ox to announce it at the temple, drew out the arrows, packed them in brocade pouches, bore them on his back at the van—and when victory came home, returned them to their place.
units.literal: Thereafter when he took the field he sent an attendant with a young ox to report at the temple, took out the arrows, placed them in brocade bags, carried them on his back riding ahead; when he returned in triumph he put them back.

units.zh: 方其係燕父子以組，函梁君臣之首，入于太廟，還矢先王而告以成功，其意氣之盛，可謂壯哉！
units.en: When he had bound the Yan princes with cord, cased the heads of Liang’s court, entered the Grand Temple, and given back the arrows to his father’s shade with news of triumph—what pride, what splendor!
units.literal: When he bound the Yan father and son with rope, boxed the heads of Liang’s lord and ministers, entered the Grand Temple, returned the arrows to the former king and reported success—his spirit at its height, one might say how magnificent!

units.zh: 及仇雠已滅，天下已定，一夫夜呼，亂者四應，蒼皇東出，未及見賊而士卒離散，君臣相顧，不知所歸，至於誓天断髮，泣下沾襟，何其衰也！
units.en: When his enemies were gone and the realm secure, a single shout in the night brought mutiny on every side; he fled east in disarray, his army melting away before he met the foe; court and emperor stared at one another with nowhere to turn, swearing to Heaven and shearing their hair, weeping until their robes were wet—how far he had fallen!
units.literal: When his foes were destroyed and the realm settled, one man cried out at night and rebels answered on four sides; he fled east in panic, before he saw the enemy his soldiers scattered; lord and ministers looked at each other not knowing where to go, until they swore to Heaven and cut their hair, tears soaking their collars—how fallen!

units.zh: 豈得之難而失之易歟？
units.en: Is it hard to win the world and easy to lose it?
units.literal: Is gaining hard and losing easy?

units.zh: 抑本其成敗之迹而皆自於人歟？
units.en: Or do success and ruin always trace back to human choices?
units.literal: Or tracing the traces of success and failure, are they all from men?

units.zh: 《書》曰：「滿招損，謙得益。」
units.en: The Book says: “Pride invites ruin; humility brings gain.”
units.literal: The Book says: “Fullness invites loss; modesty brings gain.”

units.zh: 憂勞可以興國，逸豫可以亡身，自然之理也。
units.en: Care and hardship can revive a kingdom; idleness and indulgence can destroy a man—that is the way of things.
units.literal: Anxiety and toil can raise a state; ease and pleasure can destroy oneself—nature’s principle.

units.zh: 故方其盛也，舉天下之豪傑莫能與之爭；
units.en: At his zenith no champion under Heaven could stand against him;
units.literal: Thus at his height, all the heroes under Heaven could not contend with him;

units.zh: 及其衰也，數十伶人困之，而身死國滅，為天下笑。
units.en: at his fall a handful of actors brought him down—he died, his house ended, and the world mocked him.
units.literal: at his decline, a few dozen actors beset him, and he died, the state perished, and the realm laughed.

units.zh: 夫禍患常積於忽微，而智勇多困於所溺，豈獨伶人也哉！
units.en: Disaster grows from tiny neglects; wit and valor drown in obsession—is that true only of actors?
units.literal: Calamity often gathers from the slight and minute; wisdom and courage often founder in what one drowns in—is it only actors!

units.zh: 作《伶官傳》。
units.en: Hence this “Biography of Court Entertainers.”
units.literal: [The author] composed “The Biography of Court Entertainers.”

units.zh: 莊宗既好俳優，又知音，能度曲，至今汾、晉之俗，往往能歌其聲，謂之「御製」者皆是也。
units.en: Zhuangzong loved actors, knew music, and wrote songs himself—even now in Fen and Jin people still sing his tunes; whatever is called “imperial composition” is his.
units.literal: Zhuangzong both loved actors and understood music, could compose tunes—to this day the customs of Fen and Jin often sing his melodies; what is called “imperially composed” is all his.

units.zh: 其小字亞子，當時人或謂之亞次。
units.en: His pet name was Yazi; some called him Yaci.
units.literal: His childhood name was Yazi; men of the time sometimes called him Yaci.

units.zh: 又别為優名以自目，曰李天下。
units.en: He gave himself another stage name: Li Tianxia—“Li Who Owns the World.”
units.literal: He also took a separate actor’s name for himself, calling himself Li Tianxia—“Li Who Rules All Under Heaven.”

units.zh: 自其為王，至於為天子，常身與俳優杂戲於庭，伶人由此用事，遂至於亡。
units.en: From prince to emperor he played the fool with actors in the palace yard; through them power passed into their hands—and on to destruction.
units.literal: From when he became king until he became Son of Heaven he often mixed with actors in buffoonery in the courtyard; actors thereby wielded power, until ruin.

units.zh: 皇后劉氏素微，其父劉叟，賣藥善卜，號劉山人。
units.en: Empress Liu came from nothing; her father Old Liu sold herbs and told fortunes, known as Liu the Mountain Man.
units.literal: Empress Liu was of humble birth; her father, Old Liu, sold medicine and was skilled at divination, and was called Liu the Mountain Man.

units.zh: 劉氏性悍，方與諸姬爭寵，常自恥其世家，而特諱其事。
units.en: The empress was proud and jealous, fighting the palace women for favor; she hated her low origins and hid them at all costs.
units.literal: Liu was fierce in nature; contending with the concubines for favor, she was often ashamed of her family and especially concealed the matter.

units.zh: 莊宗乃為劉叟衣服，自負蓍囊藥篋，使其子繼岌提破帽而隨之，造其卧内，曰：「劉山人来省女。」
units.en: Zhuangzong put on Old Liu’s clothes, shouldered the diviner’s pouch and medicine chest, sent his son Jiji after him in a torn cap, and walked into her chamber: “Liu the Mountain Man is here to see his girl.”
units.literal: Zhuangzong dressed as Old Liu, carried a divination bag and medicine box on his back, had his son Jiji wear a battered hat and follow, went to her bedchamber and said, “Liu the Mountain Man has come to visit his daughter.”

units.zh: 劉氏大怒，笞繼岌而逐之。
units.en: The empress erupted, beat Jiji, and threw them out.
units.literal: Liu flew into a rage, flogged Jiji, and drove them out.

units.zh: 宮中以為笑樂。
units.en: The inner court roared with laughter.
units.literal: The palace took it as a great jest.

units.zh: 其戰於胡柳也，嬖伶周匝為梁人所得。
units.en: At Huliu his beloved actor Zhou Za fell into Liang’s hands.
units.literal: At the battle of Huliu his favorite actor Zhou Za was captured by Liang.

units.zh: 其後滅梁入汴，周匝謁於馬前，莊宗得之喜甚，賜以金帛，勞其良苦。
units.en: When Liang fell and he entered Bian, Zhou Za knelt before his horse; Zhuangzong was delighted, heaped gifts on him, and praised his endurance.
units.literal: Later, having destroyed Liang and entered Bian, Zhou Za paid respects before his horse; Zhuangzong was overjoyed to have him back, bestowed gold and silks, and consoled his bitter hardship.

units.zh: 周匝對曰：「身陷仇人，而得不死以生者，教坊使陳俊、内園栽接使儲德源之力也。
units.en: Zhou Za said: “I was in the enemy’s grip and should have died—Chen Jun of the Music Bureau and Chu Deyuan of the Inner Garden saved me.
units.literal: Zhou Za replied: “Trapped among enemies yet living—I owe my life to Director of the Music Bureau Chen Jun and Inner Garden Grafting Commissioner Chu Deyuan.

units.zh: 願乞二州以報此兩人。」
units.en: Grant me two prefectures for these two men.”
units.literal: I beg two prefectures to repay these two men.”

units.zh: 莊宗皆許以為刺史。
units.en: Zhuangzong agreed to make each of them a prefect.
units.literal: Zhuangzong promised them both as regional governors.

units.zh: 郭崇韜諫曰：「陛下所與共取天下者，皆英豪忠勇之士。
units.en: Guo Chongtao objected: “The men who won the realm with you are heroes—loyal and fierce.
units.literal: Guo Chongtao remonstrated: “Those with whom Your Majesty took the realm are all heroic, loyal, brave men.

units.zh: 今大功始就，封賞未及於一人，而先以伶人為刺史，恐失天下心。
units.en: The war is barely won and not one soldier has been rewarded, yet actors are to become prefects—you will lose the army’s heart.
units.literal: Great merit has just been achieved; rewards have not yet reached a single man, yet you would first make actors regional governors—I fear losing the hearts of the realm.

units.zh: 不可！」
units.en: You must not do this!”
units.literal: It cannot be done!”

units.zh: 因格其命。
units.en: He held the edicts back.
units.literal: Thus he blocked the orders.

units.zh: 踰年，而伶人屢以為言，莊宗謂崇韜曰：「吾已許周匝矣，使吾慙見此二人。
units.en: A year later the actors pressed him again. Zhuangzong said to Guo Chongtao: “I gave Zhou Za my word—I cannot bear to meet those two men now.
units.literal: A year passed; the actors raised the matter again and again. Zhuangzong told Guo Chongtao: “I already promised Zhou Za—I would be ashamed to face these two men.

units.zh: 公言雖正，然當為我屈意行之。」
units.en: You are right—but for my sake, swallow your objections and do it.”
units.literal: Your words are correct, yet you must bend your intent and carry this out for me.”

units.zh: 卒以俊為景州刺史、德源為憲州刺史。
units.en: At last Chen Jun became prefect of Jingzhou and Chu Deyuan prefect of Xianzhou.
units.literal: In the end Jun was made prefect of Jingzhou and Deyuan prefect of Xianzhou.

units.zh: 莊宗好畋獵，獵于中牟，踐民田。
units.en: Zhuangzong loved the chase; at Zhongmou he rode through the farmers’ crops.
units.literal: Zhuangzong loved hunting; hunting at Zhongmou he trampled the people’s fields.

units.zh: 中牟縣令當馬切諫，為民請，莊宗怒，叱縣令去，將殺之。
units.en: The county magistrate seized his bridle and pleaded for his people; Zhuangzong raged, ordered him away, and prepared to execute him.
units.literal: The Zhongmou magistrate blocked his horse and urged him strongly, pleading for the people; Zhuangzong grew angry, shouted at the magistrate to leave, and was about to kill him.

units.zh: 伶人敬新磨知其不可，乃率諸伶走追縣令，擒至馬前責之曰：「汝為縣令，獨不知吾天子好獵邪？
units.en: Jing Xinmo saw the danger and rallied the actors to chase the magistrate down, drag him before the horse, and scold him: “You hold office under Heaven’s Son—do you not know he loves to hunt?
units.literal: The actor Jing Xinmo knew this could not stand; he led the other actors running after the magistrate, seized him before the horse, and rebuked him: “You are a magistrate—do you alone not know our Son of Heaven loves hunting?

units.zh: 奈何縱民稼穡以供稅賦！
units.en: Why let peasants sow grain for taxes!
units.literal: Why let the people plant grain to supply taxes and levies!

units.zh: 何不饑汝縣民而空此地，以備吾天子之馳騁？
units.en: Why not starve your whole county and clear the ground for the emperor’s horses!
units.literal: Why not starve the people of your county and empty this land to ready it for our Son of Heaven’s riding!

units.zh: 汝罪當死！」
units.en: You deserve to die!”
units.literal: Your crime deserves death!”

units.zh: 因前請亟行刑，諸伶共唱和之。
units.en: He pressed for instant punishment; the rest of the actors joined the chorus.
units.literal: He stepped forward asking for immediate execution; the other actors all chimed in.

units.zh: 莊宗大笑，縣令乃得免去。
units.en: Zhuangzong burst out laughing—and the magistrate was spared.
units.literal: Zhuangzong laughed loudly; the magistrate thereby escaped punishment.

units.zh: 莊宗嘗與羣優戲于庭，四顧而呼曰：「李天下，李天下何在？」
units.en: Once, playing with the actors in the yard, Zhuangzong glanced around and shouted: “Li Tianxia! Where is Li Tianxia?”
units.literal: Zhuangzong once played with the actors in the courtyard, looked about, and called: “Li Tianxia—where is Li Tianxia?”

units.zh: 新磨遽前以手批其頰。
units.en: Xinmo darted up and struck him across the face.
units.literal: Xinmo swiftly stepped forward and slapped his cheek.

units.zh: 莊宗失色，左右皆恐，羣伶亦大驚駭，共持新磨詰曰：「汝奈何批天子頰？」
units.en: Zhuangzong went pale; his attendants froze in terror; the actors cried out and seized Xinmo: “How dare you strike the emperor’s face?”
units.literal: Zhuangzong changed color; his attendants were all afraid; the actors were greatly alarmed and together seized Xinmo, demanding: “How dare you slap the Son of Heaven’s cheek?”

units.zh: 新磨對曰：「李天下者，一人而已，復誰呼邪！」
units.en: Xinmo answered: “There is only one Li Who Owns the World—who else did you mean?”
units.literal: Xinmo replied: “Li Who Rules All Under Heaven is but one person—who else are you calling?”

units.zh: 於是左右皆笑，莊宗大喜，賜與新磨甚厚。
units.en: The court burst into laughter; Zhuangzong was delighted and heaped gifts on Xinmo.
units.literal: Then the attendants all laughed; Zhuangzong was greatly pleased and richly rewarded Xinmo.

units.zh: 新磨嘗奏事殿中，殿中多惡犬，新磨去，一犬起逐之，新磨倚柱而呼曰：「陛下毋縱兒女嚙人！」
units.en: Reporting to the throne one day, Xinmo was set upon by the palace dogs. He clung to a pillar and yelled: “Your Majesty—control your children! They bite!”
units.literal: Xinmo once reported matters in the hall; there were many fierce dogs in the hall. As Xinmo left, one dog rose and chased him; Xinmo leaned on a pillar and called: “Your Majesty, do not let your sons and daughters bite people!”

units.zh: 莊宗家世夷狄，夷狄之人諱狗，故新磨以此譏之。
units.en: Zhuangzong’s line was Turkic; Turkic peoples shun talk of dogs—so Xinmo was needling his origin.
units.literal: Zhuangzong’s family was of barbarian descent; barbarians taboo dogs, so Xinmo used this to mock him.

units.zh: 莊宗大怒，彎弓注矢將射之，新磨急呼曰：「陛下無殺臣！
units.en: Zhuangzong snatched up his bow to shoot him; Xinmo screamed: “Do not kill me, Majesty!
units.literal: Zhuangzong was greatly angry, bent his bow, aimed an arrow, and was about to shoot; Xinmo cried urgently: “Your Majesty must not kill me!

units.zh: 臣與陛下為一体，殺之不祥！」
units.en: You and I are one—slay me and you slay yourself!”
units.literal: I and Your Majesty are one body—to kill me is ill-omened!”

units.zh: 莊宗大驚，問其故，對曰：「陛下开國，改元同光，天下皆謂陛下同光帝。
units.en: Zhuangzong stared, baffled; Xinmo said: “You founded the dynasty and named the era Tongguang—‘Shared Radiance’—so the world calls you the Emperor of Shared Radiance.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was greatly startled and asked the reason; he replied: “Your Majesty founded the state and changed the era to Tongguang; all under Heaven call Your Majesty Emperor Tongguang.

units.zh: 且同，銅也，若殺敬新磨，則同無光矣。」
units.en: Tong also means bronze—kill Jing Xinmo and you snuff out the guang in Tongguang!”
units.literal: Moreover tong means copper—if you kill Jing Xinmo, then ‘tong’ has no ‘guang’!”

units.zh: 莊宗大笑，乃釋之。
units.en: Zhuangzong roared with laughter and let him go.
units.literal: Zhuangzong laughed loudly and released him.

units.zh: 然時諸伶，獨新磨尤善俳，其語最著，而不聞其佗過惡。
units.en: Of all the actors, only Xinmo was a true master of the jest—his lines are still remembered, and no other scandal attaches to his name.
units.literal: Yet among the actors of the time only Xinmo was especially skilled at buffoonery; his wit was most renowned, and one heard no other faults from him.

units.zh: 其敗政亂國者，有景進、史彦瓊、郭門高三人為最。
units.en: The men who wrecked the realm were three: Jing Jin, Shi Yanqiong, and Men Gao.
units.literal: Those who ruined government and threw the state into chaos were foremost Jing Jin, Shi Yanqiong, and Men Gao—three men.

units.zh: 是時，諸伶人出入宫掖，侮弄縉紳，羣臣憤嫉，莫敢出氣，或反相附託，以希恩倖，四方藩鎮，貨賂交行，而景進最居中用事。
units.en: Actors wandered the inner quarters, mocking officials; the court seethed but no one spoke; some ministers flattered them for favor; governors bought their goodwill with gifts—and Jing Jin ruled from the center.
units.literal: At that time actors came and went in the inner palace, insulted and toyed with the gentry; ministers burned with resentment yet dared not breathe; some instead attached themselves seeking favor; regional commanders everywhere exchanged bribes—and Jing Jin held the most power at court.

units.zh: 莊宗遣進等出訪民間，事無大小皆以聞。
units.en: Zhuangzong sent Jin and his crew to spy on the realm; nothing was too small to reach his ear.
units.literal: Zhuangzong sent Jin and others to investigate among the people; matters large and small were all reported.

units.zh: 每進奏事殿中，左右皆屏退，軍機國政皆與參決，三司使孔謙兄事之，呼為「八哥」。
units.en: When Jin came to report, the room was cleared; he sat in on war and policy; Kong Qian of the Three Offices called him “Eighth Brother” and bowed to him like kin.
units.literal: Whenever Jin reported in the hall the attendants withdrew; military secrets and state affairs were all decided with him; Kong Qian, director of the Three Offices, treated him as an elder brother and called him “Eighth Elder Brother.”

units.zh: 莊宗初入洛，居唐故宫室，而嬪御未備。
units.en: Zhuangzong entered Luoyang and moved into the old Tang palaces, but his harem was still thin.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong first entered Luoyang he dwelt in Tang’s old palace, but his consorts were not yet sufficient.

units.zh: 閹宦希旨，多言宫中夜見鬼物，相驚恐，莊宗問所以禳之者，因曰：「故唐時，後宫萬人，今空宫多怪，當實以人乃息。」
units.en: Eunuchs told him the palace was haunted at night; he asked how to cleanse it. They said: “Tang’s inner court held ten thousand women—emptiness breeds ghosts. Put real people in the halls and the shadows will go.”
units.literal: Eunuchs currying favor said that at night ghosts were seen in the palace and all were afraid; Zhuangzong asked how to exorcise them. They said: “In old Tang the rear palace held ten thousand; now the empty halls breed spirits—fill them with living people and the hauntings will cease.”

units.zh: 莊宗欣然。
units.en: Zhuangzong liked the plan.
units.literal: Zhuangzong was pleased.

units.zh: 其後幸鄴，乃遣進等採鄴美女千人，以充後宫。
units.en: On a later visit to Ye he sent Jin and the rest to collect a thousand Ye beauties for the harem.
units.literal: Later, on an excursion to Ye, he sent Jin and others to gather a thousand beauties of Ye to fill the rear palace.

units.zh: 而進等緣以為姦，軍士妻女因而逃逸者數千人。
units.en: Jin and his men turned the roundup into rape; thousands of soldiers’ wives and daughters ran.
units.literal: But Jin and the others used the mission for debauchery; soldiers’ wives and daughters fled by the thousands.

units.zh: 莊宗還洛，進载鄴女千人以從，道路相屬，男女無别。
units.en: Returning to Luoyang, Jin marched a thousand Ye women in his train; the roads were choked, sex and order forgotten.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong returned to Luoyang, Jin loaded a thousand Ye women to follow; the road was unbroken, men and women undistinguished.

units.zh: 魏王繼岌已破蜀，劉皇后聽宦者讒言，遣繼岌賊殺郭崇韜。
units.en: Prince of Wei Jiji had taken Shu; the empress, swayed by eunuchs, ordered Jiji to murder Guo Chongtao.
units.literal: Prince of Wei Jiji had already conquered Shu; Empress Liu, listening to eunuch slander, sent Jiji to assassinate Guo Chongtao.

units.zh: 崇韜素嫉伶人，常裁抑之，伶人由此皆樂其死。
units.en: Chongtao had long hated the actors and curbed them—the actors celebrated when he died.
units.literal: Chongtao had always resented the actors and often restrained them; the actors therefore all rejoiced at his death.

units.zh: 皇弟存乂，崇韜之壻也，進讒於莊宗曰：「存乂且反，為婦翁報仇。」
units.en: Imperial brother Cunyi was Chongtao’s son-in-law; Jin whispered to Zhuangzong: “Cunyi will rise to avenge his wife’s father.”
units.literal: The imperial younger brother Cunyi was Chongtao’s son-in-law; Jin slandered him to Zhuangzong: “Cunyi is about to rebel, to avenge his father-in-law.”

units.zh: 乃囚而殺之。
units.en: They seized him and put him to death.
units.literal: He was imprisoned and killed.

units.zh: 朱友謙，以梁河中降晉者，及莊宗入洛，伶人皆求賂於友謙，友謙不能給而辭焉。
units.en: Zhu Youqian, who had brought Hezhong over from Liang, was shaken down by every actor when Zhuangzong reached Luoyang; he could not pay and refused.
units.literal: Zhu Youqian had surrendered Hezhong of Liang to Jin; when Zhuangzong entered Luoyang the actors all sought bribes from Youqian; Youqian could not pay and declined.

units.zh: 進乃讒友謙曰：「崇韜且誅，友謙不自安，必反，宜幷誅之。」
units.en: Jin accused him: “With Chongtao gone, Youqian is uneasy—he will rebel. Kill him too.”
units.literal: Jin then slandered Youqian: “Chongtao has been executed; Youqian is ill at ease and will surely rebel—he should be executed together.”

units.zh: 於是及其將五六人皆族滅之，天下不勝其冤。
units.en: Youqian and five or six of his commanders were wiped out to the last cousin; the empire groaned at the wrong.
units.literal: Thus Youqian and his generals, five or six men, were all exterminated to the clan; the realm could not bear the injustice.

units.zh: 進，官至銀青光祿大夫、檢校左散騎常侍兼御史大夫，上柱國。
units.en: Jin climbed to Silver Glory Light Grand Master, Investigating Left Regular Cavalry Attendant and Censor Grandee, Upper Pillar of State.
units.literal: Jin rose to Silver Glory Light Grand Master, Investigating Censorate Left Regular Cavalry Attendant concurrent Censor Grandee, Upper Pillar of State.

units.zh: 史彦瓊者，為武德使，居鄴都，而魏博六州之政皆決彦瓊，自留守王正言而下，皆俛首承事之。
units.en: Shi Yanqiong held Ye as Military Virtue Commissioner and ruled Weibo’s six prefectures; from Wang Zhengyan the garrison commander down, everyone kowtowed to him.
units.literal: Shi Yanqiong served as Military Virtue Commissioner at Ye; the government of Weibo’s six prefectures was all decided by Yanqiong—from garrison commander Wang Zhengyan down, all bowed and served him.

units.zh: 是時，郭崇韜以無罪見殺於蜀，天下未知其死也，第見京師殺其諸子，因相傳曰：「崇韜殺魏王繼岌而自王於蜀矣，以故族其家。」
units.en: Guo Chongtao had been murdered in Shu, but the news had not spread—only the slaughter of his sons in the capital was seen; rumor spread: “Chongtao had killed Jiji and declared himself king in Shu, and so his house was exterminated.”
units.literal: At that time Guo Chongtao was killed without crime in Shu; the realm did not know he was dead, only that the capital had killed his sons; men therefore spread the word: “Chongtao killed Prince of Wei Jiji and made himself king in Shu, and for this reason his clan was destroyed.”

units.zh: 鄴人聞之，方疑惑。
units.en: Ye buzzed with uncertainty.
units.literal: The people of Ye heard it and were full of doubt.

units.zh: 已而朱友謙又見殺。
units.en: Then Zhu Youqian was killed as well.
units.literal: Soon Zhu Youqian was also killed.

units.zh: 友謙子建徽為澶州刺史，有詔彦瓊使殺之，彦瓊秘其事，夜半馳出城。
units.en: Youqian’s son Jianhui governed Chanzhou; orders came for Yanqiong to kill him; Yanqiong hid the command and fled the city at midnight.
units.literal: Youqian’s son Jianhui was prefect of Cizhou; an edict ordered Yanqiong to kill him; Yanqiong kept the matter secret and at midnight galloped out of the city.

units.zh: 鄴人見彦瓊無故夜馳出，因驚傳曰：「劉皇后怒崇韜之殺繼岌也，已弑帝而自立，急召彦瓊計事。」
units.en: Seeing Yanqiong bolt at midnight without cause, Ye took fright and whispered: “The empress, enraged that Chongtao killed her son, has slain the emperor and seized the throne—she has called Yanqiong in haste to plot.”
units.literal: The people of Ye, seeing Yanqiong gallop out at night for no reason, panicked and spread the word: “Empress Liu, angry that Chongtao killed Jiji, has murdered the emperor and set herself up; she has urgently summoned Yanqiong to plan.”

units.zh: 鄴都大恐。
units.en: Terror seized the city.
units.literal: Ye was gripped by terror.

units.zh: 貝州人有來鄴者，傳此語以歸。
units.en: A traveler from Beizhou heard it in Ye and carried the story back.
units.literal: A man from Beizhou who had come to Ye carried this tale home.

units.zh: 戍卒皇甫暉聞之，由此劫趙在禮作亂。
units.en: Garrison soldier Huangfu Hui heard it and forced Zhao Zaili into revolt.
units.literal: The garrison soldier Huangfu Hui heard it and thereby compelled Zhao Zaili to rebel.

units.zh: 在禮已至館陶，鄴都巡檢使孫鐸，見彦瓊求兵禦賊，彦瓊不肯與，曰：「賊未至，至而給兵豈晚邪？」
units.en: Zaili was already at Guantao; Sun Duo the patrol commissioner begged Yanqiong for troops; Yanqiong refused: “The rebels aren’t here yet—why not wait until they are?”
units.literal: Zaili had already reached Guantao; Ye’s patrol commissioner Sun Duo saw Yanqiong and begged troops to resist the rebels; Yanqiong refused, saying: “The rebels have not arrived—when they come, will it be too late to issue arms?”

units.zh: 已而賊至，彦瓊以兵登北門，聞賊呼聲，大恐，棄其兵而走，單騎歸於京師。
units.en: The rebels came; Yanqiong manned the North Gate, heard their battle cries, panicked, threw down his men, and rode alone to the capital.
units.literal: Soon the rebels arrived; Yanqiong took troops to the North Gate, heard the rebels’ shouts, was greatly afraid, abandoned his soldiers and fled, alone on horseback back to the capital.

units.zh: 在禮由是得入於鄴以成其叛亂者，由彦瓊啓而縱之也。
units.en: Zaili walked into Ye and made good his revolt—because Yanqiong opened the gate and let him pass.
units.literal: Zaili was thereby able to enter Ye and complete his rebellion—from Yanqiong opening the way and letting him go.

units.zh: 郭門高者，名從謙，門高其優名也。
units.en: Men Gao was really named Congqian; Men Gao was his stage name.
units.literal: Men Gao—his name was Congqian; Men Gao was his actor’s name.

units.zh: 雖以優進，而嘗有軍功，故以為從馬直指揮使。
units.en: He had entered as an actor but once earned battle honors, so they made him commander of the Following Horse Direct.
units.literal: Though he had risen as an actor, he had once won military merit and was therefore made commander of the Following Horse Direct.

units.zh: 從馬直，蓋親軍也。
units.en: The Following Horse Direct were the emperor’s own troops.
units.literal: The Following Horse Direct was essentially the imperial guard.

units.zh: 從謙以姓郭，拜崇韜為叔父，而皇弟存乂又以從謙為養子。
units.en: Congqian was a Guo by birth and called Chongtao uncle; imperial brother Cunyi had adopted him as a son.
units.literal: Congqian bore the surname Guo and acknowledged Chongtao as uncle; the imperial younger brother Cunyi had also taken Congqian as adopted son.

units.zh: 崇韜死，存乂見囚，從謙置酒軍中，憤然流涕，稱此二人之冤。
units.en: When Chongtao was dead and Cunyi in chains, Congqian feasted his troops, wept, and cried out at the wrong done to both men.
units.literal: When Chongtao died and Cunyi was imprisoned, Congqian set wine in the army, wept in anger, and spoke of the injustice done these two men.

units.zh: 是時，從馬直軍士王溫宿衛禁中，夜謀亂，事覺被誅。
units.en: A guardsman named Wang Wen, posted in the palace, plotted mutiny by night; he was caught and killed.
units.literal: At that time the Following Horse Direct soldier Wang Wen garrisoned the forbidden precinct; at night he plotted rebellion; the plot was discovered and he was executed.

units.zh: 莊宗戲從謙曰：「汝党存乂、崇韜負我，又教王溫反。
units.en: Zhuangzong teased Congqian: “Your friends Cunyi and Chongtao betrayed me, and you set Wang Wen on the path of treason.
units.literal: Zhuangzong jested with Congqian: “Your faction—Cunyi and Chongtao—wronged me, and you taught Wang Wen to rebel.

units.zh: 復欲何為乎？」
units.en: What are you plotting now?”
units.literal: What do you plan to do next?”

units.zh: 從謙恐，退而激其軍士曰：「罄爾之貲，食肉而饮酒，無為後日計也。」
units.en: Congqian was terrified; he went back and roused his men: “Spend everything you have—feast today and leave tomorrow to chance.”
units.literal: Congqian was afraid; he withdrew and stirred his soldiers: “Empty your wealth—eat meat, drink wine, do not plan for days to come.”

units.zh: 軍士問其故，從謙因曰：「上以王溫故，俟破鄴，盡坑爾曹。」
units.en: They asked why; Congqian said: “The emperor blames you for Wang Wen—when Ye falls he will massacre every one of you.”
units.literal: The soldiers asked why; Congqian said: “Because of Wang Wen, when Ye is taken the emperor will bury you all alive.”

units.zh: 軍士信之，皆欲為亂。
units.en: They believed him—and every man was ready to rise.
units.literal: The soldiers believed it; all wished to rebel.

units.zh: 李嗣源兵反，嚮京師，莊宗東幸汴州，而嗣源先入。
units.en: Li Siyuan’s army rose and marched on the capital; Zhuangzong hurried east to Bianzhou—but Siyuan was already inside.
units.literal: Li Siyuan’s army rebelled and advanced on the capital; Zhuangzong went east in person to Bianzhou, yet Siyuan entered first.

units.zh: 莊宗至萬勝，不得進而還，軍士離散，尚有二萬餘人。
units.en: Zhuangzong reached Wansheng, could not push forward, and withdrew; the army broke apart, but he still had twenty thousand men.
units.literal: Zhuangzong reached Wansheng, could not advance and turned back; his soldiers scattered, yet more than twenty thousand remained.

units.zh: 居數日，莊宗復東幸汜水，謀扼關以為拒。
units.en: Days later he went east again to Sishui, intending to hold the pass and block his enemies.
units.literal: After several days Zhuangzong again went east in person to Sishui, planning to seize the pass as a defense.

units.zh: 四月丁亥朔，朝羣臣於中興殿，宰相對三刻罷。
units.en: On the first day of the fourth month he held court at Zhongxing Hall; the chancellors were heard for three quarters of an hour, then dismissed.
units.literal: On the first day of the fourth month, dinghai, he held court with the ministers at Zhongxing Hall; the chancellor’s audience lasted three quarters and was dismissed.

units.zh: 從駕黄甲馬軍陣於宣仁門、步軍陣於五鳳門以俟。
units.en: The imperial yellow-armor horse arrayed at Xuanren Gate and the foot at Wufeng Gate, waiting.
units.literal: The yellow-armor cavalry of the imperial escort formed ranks at Xuanren Gate and the infantry at Wufeng Gate to await events.

units.zh: 莊宗入食内殿，從謙自營中露刃注矢，馳攻興教門，與黄甲軍相射。
units.en: Zhuangzong went to eat in the inner palace; Congqian rode out of camp with blades bare and bows drawn, struck Xingjiao Gate, and traded volleys with the yellow-armor guard.
units.literal: Zhuangzong entered the inner hall to eat; Congqian from his camp bared blades and strung bows, galloped to attack Xingjiao Gate, and exchanged shots with the yellow-armor army.

units.zh: 莊宗聞亂，率諸王衛士擊亂兵出門。
units.en: Hearing the uproar, Zhuangzong led the princes and guards out to fight the mutineers.
units.literal: Zhuangzong heard the riot and led the princes and palace guards to strike the mutineers and go out the gate.

units.zh: 亂兵縱火焚門，緣城而入，莊宗擊殺數十百人。
units.en: The mutineers fired the gate and scaled the walls; Zhuangzong cut down hundreds.
units.literal: The mutineers set fire and burned the gate, climbed the wall to enter; Zhuangzong killed several hundred.

units.zh: 亂兵從楼上射帝，帝伤重，踣於絳霄殿廊下，自皇后、諸王左右皆奔走。
units.en: Mutineers rained arrows from the tower; Zhuangzong was mortally wounded and collapsed in the corridor of Jiangxiao Hall—the empress, the princes, and everyone near him ran.
units.literal: Mutineers shot the emperor from the tower; the emperor was gravely wounded and fell in the corridor of Jiangxiao Hall—empress, princes, and attendants all fled.

units.zh: 至午時，帝崩，五坊人善友聚樂器而焚之。
units.en: By noon he was dead; Shanyou of the Five Workshops heaped instruments and set them ablaze.
units.literal: By the hour of noon the emperor died; Shanyou of the Five Workshops gathered musical instruments and burned them.

units.zh: 嗣源入洛，得其骨，葬新安之雍陵。
units.en: Siyuan entered Luoyang, recovered his remains, and buried them at Yongling in Xin’an.
units.literal: Siyuan entered Luoyang, obtained his bones, and buried them at Yongling in Xin’an.

units.zh: 以從謙為景州刺史，已而殺之。
units.en: They made Congqian prefect of Jingzhou—and soon put him to death.
units.literal: Congqian was made prefect of Jingzhou, then soon executed.

units.zh: 《傳》曰：「君以此始，必以此終。」
units.en: The Commentary says: “What a lord begins with, he must end with.”
units.literal: The Commentary says: “What a ruler takes as his beginning, he will surely take as his end.”

units.zh: 莊宗好伶，而弑於門高，焚以樂器。
units.en: Zhuangzong doted on actors—yet was killed by Men Gao and consumed in a fire of instruments.
units.literal: Zhuangzong loved actors, yet was assassinated by Men Gao and burned with musical instruments.

units.zh: 可不信哉！
units.en: Who would not believe it!
units.literal: Can this fail to be believed!

units.zh: 可不戒哉！
units.en: Who would not take warning!
units.literal: Can this fail to be a warning!

units.zh: 龍德末，閑居私第將期矣，晉主入汴，振謁見首罪，郭崇韜指振謂人曰：「人言李振乃一代奇才，吾今見之，乃常人耳！」
units.en: At the end of Longde he had lived in retirement nearly a year; when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen came to beg mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at him and said: "They call Li Zhen a wonder of the age—I see an ordinary man!"
units.literal: End of Longde, living in retirement at his private residence nearly a year, when the Jin lord entered Bian, Zhen paid court asking mercy; Guo Chongtao pointed at Zhen and said to people: "People say Li Zhen is a generation's strange talent—I see him now and he is just an ordinary man!"

units.zh: 晉王遣都將李嗣昭、李存審、王建及率師來援同州，戰於城下。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji to relieve Tongzhou and battle was joined under the walls.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent commanders Li Sizhao, Li Cunshen, and Wang Jianji with troops to relieve Tongzhou; they fought below the walls.

units.zh: 夏四月己巳，晉王即唐帝位於魏州，改天祐二十年為同光元年。
units.en: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin took the Tang throne at Weizhou, renaming Tianyou 20 Tongguang 1.
units.literal: On jisi in the fourth month of summer the Prince of Jin assumed the Tang throne at Weizhou, changing Tianyou 20 to Tongguang 1.

units.zh: 時晉王方攻鎮州，故思遠乘虛以襲之，陷成安，而思遠遂急攻德勝北城，晉將李存審極力拒守。
units.en: While the Prince of Jin besieged Zhenzhou, Siyuan took Cheng'an and stormed Desheng’s north wall; Li Cunshen held firm.
units.literal: At the time the Prince of Jin was attacking Zhenzhou; hence Siyuan seized the opening to strike, took Cheng'an, and then urgently attacked Desheng’s northern city; Jin commander Li Cunshen resisted with utmost strength.

units.zh: 二月，晉王以兵至，思遠收軍而退，復保楊村。
units.en: In the second month the Prince of Jin came up; Siyuan withdrew to Yang village.
units.literal: In the second month the Prince of Jin arrived with troops; Siyuan gathered the army and withdrew, again holding Yang village.

units.zh: 唐帝棄德勝之北城，並軍保楊劉。
units.en: The Tang emperor abandoned Desheng’s north wall and concentrated at Yangliu.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor abandoned Desheng’s northern city and combined the army to hold Yangliu.

units.zh: 六月乙亥，唐帝引軍援楊劉，潛軍至博州，築壘於河東岸。
units.en: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang emperor relieved Yangliu while secretly fortifying east of Bozhou.
units.literal: On yihai in the sixth month the Tang Emperor led troops to relieve Yangliu, secretly moving the army to Bozhou and building ramparts on the river’s east bank.

units.zh: 秋七月丁未，唐帝引軍沿河而南。
units.en: On dingwei in the seventh month the Tang emperor led his army south along the river.
units.literal: On dingwei in the seventh month of autumn the Tang Emperor led troops south along the river.

units.zh: 庚寅，唐帝軍於胡城，先鋒將康延孝率百騎奔於唐，盡泄其軍機。
units.en: On gengyin at Hucheng vanguard Kang Yanxiao defected with a hundred riders and betrayed Liang dispositions.
units.literal: On gengyin the Tang Emperor’s army was at Hucheng; vanguard commander Kang Yanxiao led a hundred horsemen to defect to Tang and fully revealed our military plans.

units.zh: 甲戌，唐帝引師襲中都，王彥章兵潰，於是彥章與監軍張漢傑及趙廷隱、劉嗣彬、李知節、唐文通、王山興等皆為唐人所獲。
units.en: On jiaxu the Tang emperor stormed Zhongdu; Yanzhang’s army broke; he, Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, and others were taken.
units.literal: On jiaxu the Tang Emperor led troops to strike Zhongdu; Wang Yanzhang’s army collapsed; thereupon Yanzhang, army supervisor Zhang Hanjie, Zhao Tingyin, Liu Sibin, Li Zhijie, Tang Wentong, Wang Shanxing, and others were all captured by Tang men.

units.zh: 帝置傳國寶於臥內，俄失其所在，已為左右所竊迎唐帝矣。
units.en: He laid the seal in his chamber; it vanished—courtiers had stolen it to greet the Tang emperor.
units.literal: The Emperor placed the dynastic seal in the sleeping chamber; soon it lost its place—it had already been stolen by attendants to welcome the Tang Emperor.

units.zh: 唐帝入宮，妃郭氏號泣迎拜。
units.en: The Tang emperor entered the palace; Consort Guo wept and bowed in welcome.
units.literal: The Tang Emperor entered the palace; consort Guo wailed and came forward to bow.

units.zh: 唐帝初入東京，聞帝殂，憮然歎曰：「敵惠敵怨，不在後嗣。
units.en: Entering the Eastern Capital, the Tang emperor learned of the Last Emperor’s death and sighed: "Grudges need not pass to sons.
units.literal: When the Tang Emperor first entered the Eastern Capital and heard the Emperor had died, he sighed in dejection: "Enemy kindness and enemy hatred do not lie in later generations.

units.zh: 九月庚寅，以供奉官郎公遠充契丹歡好使。
units.en: On gengyin in the ninth month Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was sent as envoy of goodwill to the Khitan.
units.literal: On gengyin in the ninth month, Palace Attendant Lang Gongyuan was made Khitan Goodwill envoy.

units.zh: 龍德二年春正月，戴思遠率師襲魏州。
units.en: In the first month of Longde 2 Dai Siyuan raided Weizhou.
units.literal: In the first month of spring of Longde 2, Dai Siyuan led troops to raid Weizhou.

units.zh: 尋詔河南尹張全義收葬之，其首藏於太社。
units.en: He ordered Zhang Quanyi to bury the body; the head was kept at the Grand Altar.
units.literal: Soon an edict ordered Henan Intendant Zhang Quanyi to collect and bury him; his head was stored at the Grand Altar.

units.zh: 先是，繼韜父嗣昭為潞州節度使，戰歿於鎮州城下，晉王欲以嗣昭長子繼儔襲父位。
units.en: His father Li Sizhao had held Luzhou and died at Zhenzhou; the Prince of Jin meant to give the post to eldest son Jichou.
units.literal: Earlier, Jiyao’s father Sizhao was Luzhou military commissioner and fell in battle below Zhenzhou city; the Prince of Jin wished to let Sizhao’s eldest son Jichou succeed his father’s post.

units.zh: 朕與梁主十年對壘，恨不生見其面。」
units.en: We fought ten years; I regret never meeting him alive."
units.literal: I and the Liang ruler faced each other in battle ten years, regretting I did not see his face in life."

units.zh: 裨將趙在禮聞軍亂，衣不及帶，將逾垣而遁，亂兵追及，白刃環之曰：「公能為帥否？
units.en: Lieutenant Zhao Zaili, hearing the army was in chaos, had no time to belt his robe and was about to climb over the wall to flee when the mutineers caught him; blades ringed him and they said, "Can you be commander?
units.literal: Lieutenant Zhao Zaili, hearing the army in chaos, had not time to belt his robe and was about to climb the wall to flee when the mutineers overtook him; blades ringed him and they said, "Can you be commander?

units.zh: 在禮懼，即曰：「吾能為之。」
units.en: Terrified, Zhao Zaili immediately said, "I can do it."
units.literal: Terrified, Zhao Zaili immediately said, "I can do it."

units.zh: 詰旦，擁在禮趨臨清，剽永濟、館陶。
units.en: At dawn they marched Zhao Zaili toward Linqing and raided Yongji and Guantao.
units.literal: At dawn they drove Zaili toward Linqing and plundered Yongji and Guantao.

units.zh: 晡晚，趙在禮引諸軍據宮城，署皇甫暉等為都虞候、斬斫使，諸軍大掠。
units.en: By evening Zhao Zaili held the palace, made Huangfu Hui adjutant, and the army looted Ye.
units.literal: In late afternoon Zhao Zaili led the armies to seize the palace city, appointing Huangfu Hui and others overall adjutants and execution officers; the armies plundered greatly.

units.zh: 興唐尹王正言謁在禮，望塵再拜。
units.en: Wang Zhengyan bowed twice in the dust to Zhao Zaili.
units.literal: Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan called on Zaili and twice bowed in the dust.

units.zh: 是日，眾推在禮為兵馬留後，草奏以聞。
units.en: That day the mutineers made Zhao Zaili acting commissioner and memorialized court.
units.literal: That day the crowd pushed Zaili as acting military commissioner and drafted a memorial to report it.

units.zh: 辛丑，元行欽至鄴都，進攻南門，以詔書招諭城中，趙在禮獻羊酒勞軍，登城遙拜行欽曰：「將士經年離隔父母，不取敕旨歸寧，上貽聖憂，追悔何及！
units.en: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and used an edict to summon the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and bowed from the wall to Xingqin, saying, "The soldiers have been separated from their parents for years; by returning home without edict, they have burdened the sage with worry. What regret can suffice!
units.literal: On xinchou Yuan Xingqin reached Ye, attacked the south gate, and with an edict summoned the city; Zhao Zaili presented sheep and wine to comfort the army and from the wall bowed distantly to Xingqin, saying, "The troops were separated from parents for years and, not taking the edict to return home, burdened the sage—what regret can suffice!

units.zh: 眾遂呼噪，中夜燔劫貝郡。
units.en: The mutineers shouted and looted Beizhou at midnight.
units.literal: The crowd then shouted and at midnight burned and plundered Beizhou.

units.zh: 否則頭隨刃落！」
units.en: If not, your head will fall with the blade!"
units.literal: If not, your head follows the blade!"

units.zh: 儻公善為敷奏，俾從渙汗，某等亦不敢不改過自新。」
units.en: If you, sir, will memorialize well and let us follow the edict of grace, we too dare not fail to reform ourselves."
units.literal: If you, sir, will memorialize well and let us follow the edict of grace, we too dare not fail to reform."

units.zh: 軍士皇甫暉等因夜聚蒱博不勝，遂作亂，劫都將楊仁晸曰：「我輩十有餘年為國家效命，甲不離體，已至吞並天下，主上未垂恩澤，翻有猜嫌。
units.en: Soldiers Huangfu Hui and others, after losing at night gambling, mutinied and seized commander Yang Renjian, saying, "For more than ten years we have served the state, never taking armor from our bodies, until the realm was conquered; yet the sovereign has shown us no grace and instead suspects us.
units.literal: Soldiers Huangfu Hui and others, having lost at night gambling, then made rebellion and seized commander Yang Renjian, saying, "We have served the state more than ten years, armor never off our bodies, until the realm was swallowed up—yet the sovereign has not bestowed grace and instead harbors suspicion.

units.zh: 皇甫暉聚眾大詬，即壞詔。
units.en: Huangfu Hui cursed and tore up the edict.
units.literal: Huangfu Hui gathered the crowd and cursed loudly, then destroyed the edict.

units.zh: 防戍邊遠，經年離阻鄉國，及得代歸，去家咫尺，不令與家屬相見。
units.en: After years on distant frontiers, cut off from home, when they were finally relieved and came within a stone's throw of home, they were still denied even a glimpse of their families.
units.literal: Guarding distant frontiers, separated from home for years, and on relief returning home was within a foot—yet we were not allowed to see kin.

units.zh: 今聞皇后弑逆，京邑已亂，將士各欲歸府寧親，請公同行。」
units.en: Now we hear the Empress has committed regicide and the capital is in chaos; the soldiers all wish to return home to see their families. Please, sir, go with us."
units.literal: Now we hear the Empress committed regicide and the capital is in chaos; the troops each wish to return home—please, sir, go with us."

units.zh: 乃以皇子繼岌為亞獻，皇弟存紀為終獻。
units.en: Jiji was made second libationer and Cunji final libationer.
units.literal: Prince Jiji was then made second libationer and the Emperor's brother Cunji final libationer.

units.zh: 幸左龍武軍，以皇子繼岌代張全義判六軍諸衛事故也。
units.en: Cunxu visited the Left Dragon Martial Army as Prince Jiji took over Zhang Quanyi's charge of the Six Armies and Guards.
units.literal: The Emperor visited the Left Dragon Martial Army because the prince Jiji was replacing Zhang Quanyi in overseeing the Six Armies and Imperial Guards.

units.zh: 是時，帝之左右例皆奔散，唯五坊人善友斂廓下樂器簇於帝屍之上，發火焚之。
units.en: By then the Emperor's attendants had all scattered; only Shan You of the Five Workshops piled court instruments on the body and burned them.
units.literal: At this time the Emperor's attendants all fled as a rule; only Shan You of the Five Workshops gathered instruments from below the hall colonnade, piled them on the imperial corpse, and set fire.

units.zh: 是時伶人景進用事，閹官競進，故重臣憂懼，拜章請退。
units.en: The actor Jing Jin then held sway and eunuchs crowded forward, so great ministers feared for themselves and begged to step down.
units.literal: At that time the actor Jing Jin held power, and eunuchs vied for advancement; hence the great ministers were fearful and submitted memorials asking to withdraw.

units.zh: 丙申，武德使史彥瓊自鄴馳報稱：「今月六日，貝州屯駐兵士突入都城，剽劫坊市。」
units.en: On bingshen Shi Yanqiong raced from Ye to report Beizhou garrison troops had stormed the city on the sixth and looted the markets."
units.literal: On bingshen Wude commissioner Shi Yanqiong galloped from Ye to report: "On the sixth of this month soldiers garrisoned at Beizhou burst into the capital and plundered the wards and markets."

units.zh: 製以魏國夫人劉氏為皇后，仍令所司擇日備禮冊命。
units.en: Empress Liu of Wei was proclaimed and a day set for full investiture.
units.literal: A pronouncement made Lady Liu of Wei state empress and ordered the relevant office to choose a day and prepare the full investiture rite.

units.zh: 己卯，帝御文明殿，冊魏國夫人劉氏為皇后。
units.en: On jimao Cunxu enfeoffed Lady Liu of Wei as empress at Civilized Hall.
units.literal: On jimao, the Emperor attended Civilized Hall and enfeoffed Lady Liu of Wei as empress.

units.zh: 時李嗣源總帳下親軍攻東北隅；
units.en: Li Siyuan led the household guard against the northeast corner;
units.literal: Li Siyuan commanded the personal troops below the tent attacking the northeast corner;

units.zh: 李嗣源壞夾城東北隅，率先掩擊，梁軍大恐，南向而奔，投戈委甲，噎塞行路，斬萬餘級，獲其將副招討使符道昭洎大將三百人，芻粟百萬。
units.en: Li Siyuan breached Jiacity's northeast and charged in; Liang panicked and fled south, shedding arms until the road jammed; over ten thousand were killed; Fu Daozhao and three hundred officers were taken, with a million bundles of fodder.
units.literal: Li Siyuan broke the northeast corner of Jiacity and led the assault; the Liang army was greatly terrified and fled south, casting weapons and armor; the road was choked; more than ten thousand were beheaded; deputy pacification commissioner Fu Daozhao and three hundred great generals were captured, and a million measures of fodder.

units.zh: 五月辛未朔，晨霧晦暝，帝率親軍伏三垂崗下。
units.en: At the xinwei new moon in the fifth month, thick morning fog hid Cunxu's personal troops below Sanchui Ridge.
units.literal: On the first day xinwei of the fifth month, morning fog dark and dim, the Emperor led his personal army in ambush below Sanchui Ridge.

units.zh: 壬午，保義軍節度使朱友謙進百官衣二百副。
units.en: On renwu Zhu Youqian of the Baoyi Army offered two hundred sets of court robes.
units.literal: On renwu, Zhu Youqian, military governor of the Baoyi Army, presented two hundred sets of official robes.

units.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；
units.en: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
units.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;

units.zh: 以禮部尚書、興唐尹王正言依前禮部尚書，充租庸使。
units.en: Wang Zhengyan stayed Minister of Rites and was made land-tax commissioner.
units.literal: Minister of Rites and Xingtang prefect Wang Zhengyan remained Minister of Rites and was made commissioner of land tax and corvée.

units.zh: 然自此權臣愎戾，伶官用事，吏人孔謙酷加賦斂，赦文之所原放，謙復刻剝不行，大失人心，始於此矣。
units.en: Yet from then on ministers turned stubborn, actors held power, and Kong Qian re-levied what the amnesty had freed—hearts were lost from this day.
units.literal: Yet from this time powerful ministers grew obstinate, actor-officials held office, and clerk Kong Qian harshly added levies; what the amnesty had remitted Qian again exacted and would not carry out—greatly losing hearts, it began here.

units.zh: 庚午，租庸使孔謙奏：「諸道綱運客旅，多於私路苟免商稅，請令所在關防嚴加捉搦。」
units.en: On gengwu Kong Qian memorialized, "Transport convoys and traveling merchants on the circuits often evade commercial tax on private routes; order every pass and barrier to seize them strictly."
units.literal: On gengwu land-tax commissioner Kong Qian memorialized: "Transport convoys and traveling merchants on the circuits often evade commercial tax on private routes; order every pass and barrier to seize them strictly."

units.zh: 帝內殿食次，從馬直指揮使郭從謙自本營率所部抽戈露刃，至興教門大呼，與黃甲兩軍引弓射興教門。
units.en: While the Emperor dined in the inner palace, Guo Congqian, commander of the Direct Horse Corps, led his troops from camp with drawn swords to Xingjiao Gate, shouting; the Yellow Armor armies shot at the gate.
units.literal: While the Emperor was at a meal in the inner hall, Guo Congqian, commander of the Direct Horse Corps, led his men from camp with bared blades to Xingjiao Gate shouting; with the Yellow Armor two armies he drew bows and shot at Xingjiao Gate.

units.zh: 《東都事略·符彥卿傳》云：郭從謙之亂，莊宗左右皆引去，惟彥卿力戰，殺十餘人。
units.en: The 《Outline of the Eastern Capital · Fu Yanqing Biography》 says that in Guo Congqian's revolt Zhuangzong's attendants all fled; only Yanqing fought hard and killed more than ten men.
units.literal: The 《Outline of the Eastern Capital · Fu Yanqing Biography》 says: at Guo Congqian's rebellion Zhuangzong's attendants all withdrew; only Yanqing fought fiercely and killed more than ten.

units.zh: 帝聞其變，自宮中率諸王近衛禦之，逐亂兵出門。
units.en: Hearing the mutiny, the Emperor led princes and palace guards out to fight and drove the rebels from the gate.
units.literal: The Emperor heard of the mutiny, led princes and close guards from the palace to resist, and drove the rebel troops out the gate.

units.zh: 既而焚興教門，緣城而入，登宮牆歡噪，帝御親軍格鬥，殺亂兵數百。
units.en: They soon burned Xingjiao Gate, scaled the wall, and cheered from the palace ramparts; the Emperor fought with his personal guard and killed hundreds of rebels.
units.literal: Soon they burned Xingjiao Gate, climbed in along the wall, mounted the palace ramparts shouting in joy; the Emperor led his personal guard in hand-to-hand combat and killed several hundred rebels.

units.zh: 以前安國軍節度副使、檢校太保、左衛上將軍李存乂為晉州節度使、檢校太傅；
units.en: former Anguo Army deputy military governor, honorary Grand Guardian, and Left Guard senior general Li Cunyi became military governor of Jin Prefecture and honorary Grand Mentor;
units.literal: former Anguo deputy commissioner, Grand Guardian, and General of the Left Guards Li Cunyi was made Jinzhou military commissioner and Grand Mentor;

units.zh: 教坊伶官敬新磨受賄，為人告，帝令御史台征還其錢而後撻之。
units.en: Jing Xinmo of the music office took bribes; Mingzong had the censorate recover the cash and then flog him.
units.literal: Music-office performer Jing Xinmo took bribes; someone reported it; the Emperor ordered the Censorate to recover the money and then flog him.

units.zh: 后父劉叟，黃鬚，善醫卜，自號劉山人。
units.en: Her father, Old Liu, had a yellow beard, practiced medicine and divination, and called himself the Mountain Man Liu.
units.literal: The empress’s father, Old Liu, had yellow whiskers, was skilled in medicine and divination, and styled himself the Mountain Man Liu.

units.zh: 后生五六歲，晉王攻魏，掠成安，裨將袁建豐得后，納之晉宮，貞簡太后教以吹笙歌舞。
units.en: At five or six she was taken when the Prince of Jin raided Cheng’an; Yuan Jianfeng brought her to the Jin palace, where Dowager Zhenjian taught her music and dance.
units.literal: When the empress was five or six, the Prince of Jin attacked Wei and raided Cheng’an; the lieutenant Yuan Jianfeng took her and brought her into the Jin palace, where Empress Dowager Zhenjian taught her to play the sheng and to sing and dance.

units.zh: 五日晚，有自貝州來者，言亂兵將犯都城，都巡檢使孫鐸等急趨史彥瓊之第，告曰：「賊將至矣，請給鎧仗，登陴拒守。」
units.en: On the fifth evening, someone arrived from Bei Prefecture saying the rebel troops were about to attack the capital; patrol commissioner Sun Duo and others hurried to Shi Yanqiong's residence and told him, "The rebels are about to arrive. Please issue armor and weapons so we can mount the walls and defend them."
units.literal: On the evening of the fifth someone came from Beizhou saying the mutineers would attack the capital; capital patrol commissioner Sun Duo and others hurried to Shi Yanqiong's residence and reported, "The rebels are coming—please issue armor and weapons and mount the walls to defend."

units.zh: 孫鐸曰：「賊來寇我，必倍道兼行，一朝失機，悔將何及！
units.en: Sun Duo said, "When rebels come to attack us they will surely march by forced stages; if we lose the moment once, what regret will suffice!
units.literal: Sun Duo said, "When rebels come to attack us they surely march by forced stages; lose the moment once and what regret will suffice!

units.zh: 時彥瓊疑孫鐸等有他誌，故拒之。
units.en: He suspected Sun Duo's motives and rejected the plan.
units.literal: At the time Yanqiong suspected Sun Duo and others of other designs, hence he refused them.

units.zh: 遲明，亂軍入城，孫鐸與之巷戰，不勝，攜其母自水門而出，獲免。
units.en: At dawn mutineers entered; Sun Duo fought in the streets, then escaped with his mother through the water gate.
units.literal: At daybreak the mutineers entered the city; Sun Duo fought them in the lanes but could not win; he took his mother out through the water gate and escaped.

units.zh: 請僕射率眾登陴，鐸以勁兵千人伏於王莽河逆擊之；
units.en: He asked Shi Yanqiong to hold the wall while he ambushed a thousand elite troops at Wangmang River.
units.literal: Please, Vice Director, lead the masses onto the walls; Duo will lie in ambush with a thousand crack troops at Wangmang River to strike them head-on;

units.zh: 賊既挫勢，須至離潰，然後可以剪除。
units.en: A river ambush would break them before they reached the wall.
units.literal: once the rebels' momentum is broken they must scatter—then they can be cut down.

units.zh: 如俟其凶徒薄於城下，必慮奸人內應，則事未可測也。」
units.en: If we wait until the wicked host presses the wall, we must fear traitors within, and then the matter cannot be predicted."
units.literal: If we wait until the wicked host presses the wall, we must fear traitors within—and then the affair cannot be gauged."

units.zh: 甲午，從馬直宿衛軍士王溫等五人夜半謀亂，殺本軍使，為衛兵所擒，磔於本軍之門。
units.en: On jiawu five palace guards led by Wang Wen killed their officer at midnight, were caught, and dismembered at the camp gate.
units.literal: On jiawu followers-of-the-horse direct palace guard soldiers Wang Wen and five others plotted rebellion at midnight, killed their army commander, were seized by guards, and were dismembered at their army's gate.

units.zh: 晉王兵擊王行瑜，承業數往來兵間，晉王喜其為人。
units.en: When the Prince of Jin campaigned against Wang Xingyu, Chengye shuttled among the armies; the Prince of Jin took a liking to him.
units.literal: When the Prince of Jin’s army attacked Wang Xingyu, Chengye went back and forth among the troops many times; the Prince of Jin was pleased with his character.

units.zh: 晉王憐承業，不忍殺，匿之斛律寺。
units.en: The Prince of Jin spared Chengye and hid him at Hulu Temple.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin pitied Chengye and would not kill him, hiding him at Hulu Temple.

units.zh: 晉王病且革，以莊宗屬承業曰：「以亞子累公等。」
units.en: As the Prince of Jin lay dying he entrusted Zhuangzong to Chengye: “I place Yazi in your hands.”
units.literal: The Prince of Jin, gravely ill, entrusted Zhuangzong to Chengye, saying: “I leave Yazi in your charge.”

units.zh: 其後，梁兵攻仁恭，仁恭遣居翰從晉王攻梁潞州以牽其兵，晉遂取潞州，以居翰為昭義監軍。
units.en: Later, when Liang attacked Rengong, Rengong sent Juhan with the Prince of Jin against Liang's Luzhou to draw off Liang's army; Jin took Luzhou and appointed Juhan Zhaoyi army supervisor.
units.literal: Later, when Liang troops attacked Rengong, Rengong sent Juhan to follow the Prince of Jin in attacking Liang's Luzhou to draw off their forces; Jin then took Luzhou and made Juhan army supervisor of Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 承業起，持莊宗衣而泣，曰：「臣受先王顧托之命，誓雪家國之讎。
units.en: Chengye seized his sleeve and wept: “Your father entrusted you to me—I swore to avenge our house and state.
units.literal: Chengye rose, seized Zhuangzong’s robe, and wept: “Your servant received the late king’s dying charge and swore to wipe out the realm’s enemy.

units.zh: 今日為王惜庫物而死，死不愧於先王矣！」
units.en: If I die today guarding this storehouse, I die with a clear conscience before your father!”
units.literal: Today I die guarding the vault for the King—I die with no shame before the late king!”

units.zh: 臣，唐家一老奴耳，誠願見大王之成功，然後退身田里，使百官送出洛東門，而令路人指而嘆曰『此本朝敕使，先王時監軍也』，豈不臣主俱榮哉？」
units.en: I am only an old slave of Tang. Let me see you triumph, then go home while officials see me out Luoyang’s east gate and folk point and say, “That was the late king’s commissioner”—would not we both be glorified?”
units.literal: Your servant is but an old slave of the Tang house and truly wishes to see the Great King succeed, then retire to the fields, have the hundred officials escort him out Luoyang’s east gate, and let passersby point and sigh, “There goes the dynasty’s commissioner, army supervisor in the late king’s day”—would not lord and minister both be honored?”

units.zh: 承業方臥病，聞之，自太原肩輿至魏，諫曰：「大王父子與梁血戰三十年，本欲雪家國之讎，而復唐之社稷。
units.en: Chengye was bedridden; hearing this he was carried from Taiyuan to Wei and pleaded: “Father and son bled against Liang for thirty years to avenge Tang and restore the dynasty.
units.literal: Chengye lay ill; hearing it, he was carried by sedan from Taiyuan to Wei and remonstrated: “King and son have fought Liang in blood for thirty years, intending to avenge house and state and restore Tang’s altars.

units.zh: 自貞簡太后、韓德妃、伊淑妃及諸公子在晉陽者，承業一切以法繩之，權貴皆斂手畏承業。
units.en: Empress Dowager Zhenjian, the consorts Hande and Yishu, the princes at Jinyang—Chengye held them all to the law, and the great families learned to fear him.
units.literal: From Empress Dowager Zhenjian, Consort Hande, Consort Yishu, and all the princes at Jinyang, Chengye bound every one by law; the powerful all shrank back in fear of him.

units.zh: 盧質嗜酒傲忽，自莊宗及諸公子多見侮慢，莊宗深嫉之。
units.en: Lu Zhi drank hard and treated everyone with contempt; Zhuangzong and the princes smarted under it, and the emperor hated him for it.
units.literal: Lu Zhi was fond of wine and arrogant; from Zhuangzong down to the princes many were insulted by him, and Zhuangzong deeply resented it.

units.zh: 曆鄜州節度使，後以郭崇韜婿為莊宗所殺。
units.en: He had served as military commissioner of Fuzhou and was later executed by Zhuangzong for being Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.
units.literal: He successively served as military commissioner of Fuzhou and was later killed by Emperor Zhuangzong because he was Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.

units.zh: 〈（《北夢瑣言》云：莊宗異母弟存乂，以郭崇韜女婿伏誅。
units.en: (Beimeng Suoyan records that Cunyi, Zhuangzong's half-brother, was put to death for being married to Guo Chongtao's daughter.
units.literal: (Beimeng Suoyan states: Cunyi, Emperor Zhuangzong's younger brother by a different mother, was executed because he was Guo Chongtao's son-in-law.
